To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiency for the assessment of a bulk sample by gamma-ray spectroscopy is a linear function of the mass fraction of the sample material in the sample holder, and the slope of the efficiency versus mass fraction curve depends on the intrinsic inhomogeneities of the sample and the sample holder.
the efficiency for the assessment of the inhomogeneous bulk sample is higher than that for the equivalent homogeneous sample.
the effect of the intrinsic sample inhomogeneity on the efficiency for a measurement of the sample is negligible.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: what is the difference between the efficiency of a measurement of an inhomogeneous sample (with a known spatial distribution of the activity) and the efficiency of a sample made from a matrix equivalent to the inhomogeneous one.
the following problem: how to estimate the efficiency of a sample of a certain size and shape made from the homogeneous material with a known composition.

the following problems: the effect of the sample's intrinsic inhomogeneity on the efficiency of its measurement by gamma-ray spectrometer; the influence of the inhomogeneity on a sample's response function, which is a key element of gamma-ray spectrometric analysis; and the influence of the sample inhomogeneity on gamma-ray spectrometrical calibration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the efficiency of an inhomogeneous sample differs from that of a sample made from equivalent homogeneous matrix by a value of the order of a few percent.
the difference is small and the use of the efficiency for the homogeneous sample as a substitute for the efficiency for the sample under study is justified.

the effect of the inhomogeneity of the bulk sample on the measurement efficiency is negligible, and therefore the efficiency for an equivalent homogeneous sample can be used for the calculation of the activity concentration of the inhomogeneous bulk sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the difference is small, and that the efficiency for an inhomogeneous sample is approximately equal to the efficiency for a homogeneous sample of the same mass.
the effect of sample heterogeneity can be neglected for most practical purposes.
the effect of the inhomogeneity of the bulk sample on the measurement efficiency is negligible for samples that are large in comparison with the size of the detector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of the inhomogeneity is not negligible for the samples of small mass.

the efficiency for the bulk sample can be approximated by the efficiency for the equivalent homogeneous matrix with a relative error of 1% or less for a wide range of sample geometries and for a wide range samples with different compositions and sizes.
the effect of the inhomogeneity is not negligible and should be taken into consideration when assessing the bulk samples.
